description: HEXARA is a team of six students passionate about space, technology, and innovation. We’re building health-monitoring software for astronauts and love turning ideas into practical solutions. We’re looking for teammates skilled or interested in programming, UI/UX, AI/data, health or space science, research, and presentation. Most importantly, we value creativity, teamwork, curiosity, and a willingness to learn!
summary: OrbitWell is a space-themed wellbeing companion for astronaut health, built for astronauts, trainees, and post-mission users. It combines simulated wearable data, personal trends, movement awareness, wellbeing guidance, and NASA educational resources in one clear, accessible dashboard. Users can connect stage-appropriate wearables and review signals like heart rate, heart-rate variability, sleep, oxygen saturation, skin temperature, and radiation exposure. Trends appear only once all required devices are connected, helping build a more reliable personal baseline. Users can also do guided movement practices via on-device body tracking, which measures motion patterns such as repetitions, joint-angle ranges, pauses, and consistency without storing video. OrbitWell includes the ORBIT chatbot for NASA, space, and general health questions. It offers referenced educational information while clearly noting that its responses are not medical diagnoses or operational authority. The app also includes offline-friendly behavior, privacy-focused local processing, data-quality indicators, and clear explanations when information is incomplete or unavailable. OrbitWell meets the challenge by making complex astronaut-health information understandable and actionable. This matters because it encourages early awareness, supports personal preparation, protects user privacy, and helps astronauts communicate more effectively with approved medical or mission-support teams.
details:
Our project is an AI-powered, human-centered health companion for astronauts in training, active and former astronauts, and ground health teams. The platform tracks six key indicators using simulated data or information from connected wearables and personal dosimeters. It compares readings with each astronaut’s personal patterns, highlights meaningful changes, tracks movement, supports wellbeing check-ins, and gives personalized guidance.

The platform tracks six health indicators: heart rate, HRV, SpO₂, skin temperature, sleep, and radiation dose using simulated or connected wearable data It compares readings with personal patterns, flags changes, tracks movement, supports wellbeing check-ins, and offers personalized guidance. ORBIT, its AI assistant, helps users explore trusted space research and reflect on their experiences.

This project helps users explore trusted space research and reflect on their experiences, helping astronauts see their health beyond single numbers and encouraging earlier awareness, communication, and ongoing support.

We built it with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Three.js, Supabase, MediaPipe, Vapi, and NASA’s DONKI API. It supports wearables, Bluetooth heart-rate sensors, dosimeters, imported files, and camera-based movement tracking.

Our project is creative because we combine health monitoring, movement analysis, wellbeing, space-weather context, and trusted research in one stage-specific platform.

We considered privacy, accessibility, data quality, missing readings, individual differences, and safety. The app does not diagnose conditions or replace medical and mission professionals.
